segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: Let’s go through the Acme onboarding research and focus on the biggest friction points.

segments.speaker: Nora
segments.text: The clearest issue was team invitations. Several people were unsure whether they had successfully invited a teammate.

segments.speaker: Omar
segments.text: We also saw users land in an empty workspace and hesitate because they didn’t know what to do first.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: So invites are the first problem, and the second is the empty first-run experience.

segments.speaker: Nora
segments.text: People responded much better when we showed them an example workspace with a few guided steps.

segments.speaker: Omar
segments.text: I think we should cut the onboarding checklist down. Five steps feels heavy before users see value.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: Let’s make it three steps: create workspace, invite teammate, choose a starter template.

segments.speaker: Nora
segments.text: I’ll prototype a guided setup flow using those three steps.

segments.speaker: Omar
segments.text: I can update the first-run checklist and remove the lower-value setup tasks.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: For the next research session, let’s compare the simple checklist against the guided flow.

segments.speaker: Nora
segments.text: We should track whether users reach their first useful meeting recap faster.

segments.speaker: Omar
segments.text: And measure invite completion separately because that’s clearly a drop-off point.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: Great. Let’s run that follow-up usability test next week.
